title: Gimme Credit
summary:
In 2022, investors who feared the Fed's rate increases would bring on a recession caused
the average high yield bond price to incorporate risk protection in the form of a yield spread
of more than 4%, Over time, investors also became less worried about a possible recession, and this led to
reduced insistence on generous risk protection via credit spreads. Increased demand, lower interest rates, and reduced insistence on risk protection in the form
of higher spreads, is a perfect formula for price appreciation, and it ensued.

reader_summary.headline: The questions I get from clients enable me to understand in real time what's on their minds.
reader_summary.overview: The questions I get from clients enable me to understand in real time what's on their minds. At various points in the last ten years, the most frequently asked question was, when will the Fed raise or cut rates? During crises it's usually what inning are we in?

key_points.text: And in the last few months it's, what about spreads?

key_points.text: Ever since interest rates got up off the floor, in 2022 there's been increased interest in credit.
key_points.evidence_quote: Ever since interest rates got up off the floor, in 2022 there's been increased interest in credit, and that's why I'm devoting this memo to it.

key_points.text: It will come a little closer than usual to talking my book, but I think the subject justifies that.
